title: Which kinds of question should never get an "always use this answer" choice?
context: Our own rules say a spec change raised during development is always asked straight away, and four more kinds of question marked hard to undo are still allowed: architecture path, spec contradiction, analytics naming violations and new analytics events. A standing answer would decide these with nobody looking. Recommended: the four listed plus spec changes and every kind marked hard to undo, nine in all, which widens AC-10 from four to nine. These are the questions where an unseen wrong answer costs most, and the earlier answer still shows as a one-click suggestion, so the person only loses the skip.
